notes.1: Includes the need to get records of roasts already completed (temperatures, times) into the app from the software that logged them, so they aren't re-typed by hand. Does not include loading a profile or curve to roast against next time, which is a target rather than a record of a past roast and belongs under "Roast against a profile I trust". The source software or file type doesn't decide this; what the data is for does.
notes.2: Includes needing a target roast profile to follow during a roast so the curve can be repeated, regardless of where the profile comes from (e.g. loaded from roasting software like Artisan). Does not include getting records of roasts already done into the app, which belongs to "Stop re-typing roasts from my roasting software".
notes.3: Includes needs to take my own roast and brew data out of the app in a format other tools can read, as a one-off export for analysis elsewhere or as a backup against losing it, including saving a full copy somewhere I control. Does not include bringing someone else's shared recipe in as my own editable copy, even if the Request uses the word "export"; that belongs under "Keep my own copy of a recipe someone shared". Does not include keeping another tool automatically up to date as I log, which belongs under "Keep my other tools up to date as I log".
notes.4: Includes needs to take a recipe someone else shared and keep it as my own editable copy so I can tweak it without changing the original, even if the request words it as "export". Does not include getting my own data out of the app, which belongs to "Get my data out of the app".
notes.5: Includes the need to recall the grinder setting previously used for each bean and brew method so the user starts from a known good setting rather than guessing. Does not include saved settings becoming inaccurate because servicing, such as fitting new burrs, changed what the dial numbers mean; that belongs to "Keep grind settings meaningful after servicing the grinder". It assumes the dial's meaning stays constant.
notes.6: Includes needs where servicing the grinder (cleaning, changing burrs, recalibrating) changes what saved grind numbers mean, so past settings and notes stop being reliable. Does not include simply recalling a past setting when the dial still means the same thing ("Start from the grind setting that worked"). Does not include coffee retained in the grinder between doses, which is about coffee in versus coffee out and belongs to "Account for coffee that stays in the grinder".
notes.7: Includes needs about the gap between coffee put into the grinder and coffee that comes out, such as retained grounds, so doses and ratios are accurate. Does not include what grind setting numbers mean or how they shift after servicing or recalibrating, which belongs to "Keep grind settings meaningful after servicing the grinder".
notes.8: Includes the need to see remaining green (unroasted) coffee stock decrease as I roast, so I know when to reorder from the importer. Does not include tracking roasted coffee on the shelf or resting after roasting, which belongs to "Know how much roasted coffee is left".
notes.9: Includes needing the right water amount for a given coffee dose and ratio, including scaling a recipe up or down (e.g. halving for one cup) while keeping its ratio. Does not include tracking or logging brew results, or choosing which ratio or recipe to use in the first place.
notes.10: Includes knowing how much roasted coffee remains on the shelf, including each roast's batch still resting, so I can plan the next roast before running out. Does not include tracking unroasted green coffee stock, which is about reordering from the importer and belongs under "Know how much green coffee I have left".
notes.11: Includes the need for what I log here to appear automatically in other tools I use, so they stay current without manual exporting. Does not include one-off exports or backups of my data, which belong under "Get my data out of the app". Does not include simply pulling data out on demand, since the focus here is ongoing sync as I log.
